source.title: Weight Decay Regimes in Grokking Transformers: Cheap Online Diagnostics

record.tranche_reason: It trains models on modular arithmetic and measures grokking under varied training conditions, using a setup the text describes as following the canonical Power et al. baseline. It is not presented as an explicit replication.
record.gate_note: Rows cover reported grokking rates, times, and weight-decay transitions. The attention similarity and entropy diagnostics are not rows for V2: the authors say they measure head coordination/differentiation, not which algorithm heads compute or whether memorizing components are removed. The paper cites results from other work, but those are not included as rows. It does not vary training-set size or test non-algorithmic data.
record.test_reason: The study trains Power-style transformers, plus MLP, LSTM and Mamba networks, on p=97 modular arithmetic. It reports grokking rates and time-to-grok across weight decay, tasks and architectures. This bears on whether algorithmic grokking occurs (V1) and whether weight decay controls the move from memorization to generalization (V5). It does not vary training-set size, report train-accuracy saturation timing, identify circuits, or compare optimizers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. Weight decay acts as an empirical control parameter separating memorization, developmental-grokking and collapse regimes in modular arithmetic. The critical weight decay is λc≈0.0158 for the canonical transformer, with time-to-grok exponent ν≈0.757, and λc varies roughly tenfold across architectures. The attention diagnostics track staged coordination and differentiation but are correlational, apart from a head-reinitialization effect on Phase-2 amplitude. The authors claim no universality class or mechanism and limit scope to modular arithmetic.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a modular-arithmetic grokking setup described as following the canonical Power baseline, but expands the weight-decay, task, scale, and architecture sweeps and adds online attention diagnostics; it is not described as an explicit replication.
record.method_sensitivity: Grokking rates and fitted transition weight decays vary with weight decay, task, architecture, model scale, and training horizon. The paper reports different λc fits across architecture configurations and distinguishes the long-horizon retention outcomes by seed.

fits_no_version.finding: Generalization after grokking can collapse late in training in a seed-dependent way. Over 20K epochs, retention was 5/5, 4/5, 3/5 and 4/5 at λ=0.1, 0.5, 1.0 and 2.0; seed 42 dropped to 0.46 test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-stage loss of generalization after grokking (anti-grokking) is seed-dependent and more frequent at higher weight decay.

record.problems: The study fixes the training split at half of the modular-arithmetic examples, so it cannot establish that shrinking the training set lengthens the delay. Training-accuracy saturation is not separately reported in the experimental outcome summaries. The authors note that the weight-decay grid is too sparse for full finite-size data collapse, that some per-task medium-scale comparisons are under-powered, and that cross-architecture comparisons are not strictly parameter-matched. Several late-stage trajectory claims are based on a small five-seed cohort.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for attention similarity, entropy standard deviation, head clusters, or participation ratio: these are diagnostics of head dynamics, not measurements of the algorithm-specific circuit or cleanup named in V2. The per-head-dimension amplitude, intervention contrasts, and retention-classifier results were also left out because they do not measure the delayed-generalization or efficiency claims directly. The reported large-scale collapse (85 M at λ=1.0) was left out because it is outside the small-network setting of the versions tested here.

untested.parts: The delay growing as the training set shrinks: the split is fixed at 50%. The timing of train-accuracy saturation relative to the test-accuracy jump is not reported.
The critical dataset size and ungrokking below it; evidence that a more efficient generalizing circuit is the cause.
Not tested. The attention diagnostics measure head redundancy, not circuit formation or cleanup.
Not tested: algorithmic data only, and no initialization-scale manipulation.
Not tested. The algorithm is not identified.
Not tested. AdamW is fixed; other optimizers are deferred.

missing.what: The 85M transformer at λ=1.0 collapses to a null state (s̄=1.000) by epoch 3000 instead of grokking, a scale dependence of grokking on algorithmic data
Additional Mamba probes: expand-2 on mod+ (42/70 grok, λc=0.0163) and mod× (37/70 grok, λc=0.0191)
Per-cell grok rates by task, scale and weight decay (e.g. mod− 5/5 at λ≥0.05)

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source. Grokking is detected by a test-accuracy threshold; train-accuracy curves are not reported, so the 'long after saturation' part of V1 rests on the setup, not on measured numbers. Weight-decay control bears on V5's low-norm-bias part only; there is no dataset-size or ungrokking test. Cross-architecture differences in λc do not limit V5, which does not claim a universal threshold. The retention rows were moved out of V1.

versions.untested_parts: Training accuracy saturation is not separately reported as an outcome in the experimental results; training-set size is fixed at half the examples, so the effect of shrinking the training set on delay is not tested.

The paper measures attention-head coordination and differentiation, but does not identify a generalizing circuit, test Fourier computation, measure removal of memorizing components, or show that these diagnostics anticipate the test-accuracy jump.
The reported tasks are modular arithmetic; the paper does not test images, text, molecules, or a lazy-to-rich transition switched through initialization scale or weight norm.
No LLM pretraining or realistic-data fine-tuning is studied.
The paper varies weight decay and measures grokking regimes, but does not vary dataset size or establish that a more efficient generalizing circuit causes the observed transitions.
The paper does not identify the algorithm learned across runs or test whether runs converge to the same algorithm.
The paper uses AdamW but does not compare optimizer or numerical choices to test whether they produce or remove the delay.

relation.reason: The study reports its own training experiments measuring grokking across weight decay, tasks, model sizes and architectures.

tranche.reason: The canonical experiments follow the Power-style modular-arithmetic transformer setup and measure grokking occurrence and time-to-grok; additional sweeps extend this replication.

source_check.notes: The numerical extractions match the text. Canonical and pooled decay thresholds use different protocols; the study does not measure training-fraction dependence, post-saturation delay, or the full circuit-efficiency account.
